items.stem: Why can last-touch attribution overstate a channel's value?

options.text: It credits the final touchpoint with the whole outcome, ignoring earlier influences
options.rationale: Correct: last-touch assigns all credit to the last interaction.
It misallocates credit rather than undercounting totals.
Attribution is not the same as incrementality.

options.text: It cannot be tracked with UTMs
options.rationale: UTMs support, not prevent, last-touch tracking.

items.explanation: Correct: last-touch assigns all credit to the last interaction.

items.stem: Which TWO metrics best reflect long-term marketing health rather than vanity? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: CLV captures long-term value per customer.
Correct: retention shows whether customers stay and keep paying.
Impressions do not show value or action.
Likes are a vanity metric with weak link to value.

items.explanation: Correct: CLV captures long-term value per customer.

items.stem: Spend and sales both rose during a campaign. What is the safest conclusion?

options.text: The rise may be partly seasonal or coincidental; an experiment is needed to show incrementality
options.rationale: Correct: correlation during a campaign does not prove the spend caused the sales.

options.text: The spend definitely caused all the extra sales

options.rationale: That is equally unsupported without a test.
Attribution allocates credit, it does not prove causation.
